title: Conway's Game of Life
subject: Mathematics
author: Dan McCreary
learningObjectives: State the four transition rules of the Game of Life: underpopulation below 2 neighbors, survival at 2 or 3, overpopulation above 3, and reproduction at exactly 3
Calculate the next state of a cell by counting its 8 neighbors and applying the rules, then verify the result using the Step button
Identify the blinker, glider, block, and beehive, and classify each as an oscillator, spaceship, or still life
Predict the fate of a hand-drawn pattern before pressing Start, and revise the prediction from the generations that follow
Explain how emergent complexity such as a glider's diagonal travel arises from purely local neighbor rules with no global controller
